stories.stat_label: giant wētā released to new homes
stories.headline: A hand-sized insect bounced back from just 1 island
stories.summary: By the 1990s wētāpunga, NZ's heaviest insect, survived only on Little Barrier Island. Zoos then bred tens of thousands, and last year 11,000 went to predator-free islands and sanctuaries.
stories.why: It moved from Endangered to Recovering, helped by local iwi and community fundraisers.

stories.headline: Elephants 'sing' in chorus to agree on what to do next
stories.summary: Using machine learning on 902 recordings of 84 wild elephants, scientists found rumbles in group choruses grow more alike as elephants greet each other or plan their next move.
stories.why: About 60% of elephant rumbles happen in choruses, and we're starting to decode them.

stories.headline: Indian physicists find a superconductor that breaks the rules
stories.summary: A team at IISER Bhopal grew crystals of YbSb₂ and probed them with muons. It's the first 'type I' superconductor seen making its own tiny magnetic fields as it starts to superconduct.
stories.why: It hints at exotic quantum states in a kind of material once thought to be well understood.

stories.headline: 20 English coins reveal medieval Rome's 'Little England'
stories.summary: Digs beside the Vatican found 19 silver pennies and a halfpenny from 10th-century England, plus craft workshops: the first physical trace of an English quarter that may have housed hundreds.
stories.why: It suggests English visitors could spend their own money in Rome, a rare perk.

fun_fact: An adult female wētāpunga can fill the palm of your hand.
